text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a regression in slab-batcher run last night after the kernel-selection tweak. batch_util dropped from ~0.78 to ~0.46 and token/s across the stack is down. KV cache evictions spiked at 03:12 UTC. Anyone on this? :eyes:

derrick: Seen it. I have the profiler dump from the test infra. attaching short excerpt. looks like more small micro-batches forming and our kernel fallback is triggering more often.

li: Can you paste the profiler excerpt inline? quick triage: is it batching policy or queue shaping?

derrick: Paste: ```
# simplified sample from perf viewer
batch_formation_ms: 2.3 -> 5.8
mean_batch_size: 11.2 -> 6.1
kernel_choice: fused_attn -> safe_attn_fallback (40% -> 72%)
kvcache_evictions/min: 3 -> 18
tokens/sec/node: 42.3k -> 24.7k
```

arjun: That lines up with the windowing change we rolled — the new "slab" window reduces max coalescing window by 40% for short tails. It may be prematurely flushing queues for low-latency SLOs and increasing fallback kernels because of different seq_len distribution.

maya: Ops-bot, link the job and the dashboard panels for last 4h so we can annotate.

ops-bot: <link to job run id=run-2026-04-02-03> Dashboard: <link to dashboards/slab-batcher-telemetry> :white_check_mark:

sasha: Quick ask — do we have per-model seq_len histograms aligned with kernel selection? If short sequences are now overrepresented we'll see safe_attn picked more.

li: I pulled the seq_len slice for the window: ```json
{"p50": 32, "p90": 96, "p99": 256, "mean": 78, "count": 1240000}
```
post-change p90 moved from 72 -> 96. More long tails but also more tiny sequences causing fragmentation.

derrick: Hypothesis: the slab window increases queue churn for short requests, so effective batch packing drops and kernel heuristics pick conservative kernels based on increased variance in seq_len within a batch. That increases runtime overhead and triggers more KV cache misses due to different KV lifetimes.

maya: Proposed quick remediations: 1) revert slab window tweak for canary region, 2) enable conservative batch padding for small windows (pad to median within 50ms), 3) add dashboard panel for "kernel fallback rate" and "kvcache_eviction_rate" per-model. Thoughts?

arjun: +1 on canary revert. Also we should add a sampled trace that captures: batch formation timeline, per-request seq_len, chosen kernel, and kvcache hits/evictions. Sample 1/500 so low overhead.

sasha: I'll add the panels. Minimal panels to add: batch_utilization (per instance), mean_batch_size, queue_depth over window, kernel_fallback_pct, kvcache_evictions/min, tokens_per_sec. Also add an alert: kernel_fallback_pct > 30% for 5m.

li: For tracing, here's a snippet to emit from runtime: ```yaml
telemetry_samples: 1/500
emit_fields: [batch_id, batch_start_ms, batch_end_ms, seq_lens, kernel, kvcache_hits, kvcache_evictions]
metric_tags: [model, region, instance_type]
```

derrick: I ran a quick local sim with pad-to-median=50ms and it raises mean_batch_size back to ~9.8 and tokens/sec to ~38k. Kernel fallback drops to ~28%. Not perfect but much closer.

maya: Good — schedule a rollback for the canary slab window in the next deploy window and push the pad-to-median flag behind a feature flag for runtime tuning. I'll own the rollout.

ops-bot: Created rollout ticket T-4628 and canary revert PR: <link-to-pr>. Added dashboard task to S-123.

arjun: Long term: we should have an automated heuristic that picks batching window based on short-term seq_len variance and expected KV-cache lifetime. Put it on the perf roadmap.

maya: Agree. Action items: derrick -> attach profiler trace + sample IDs; sasha -> new dashboards + alert; li -> add telemetry sampling config PR; arjun -> design doc for adaptive windowing. I'll file a postmortem if rollback doesn't fully recover.

derrick: Attach: run-2026-04-02-03-profiler.tar.gz (uploaded to run artifacts). I'll also dump the slow-path kernel traces.

sasha: Dashboards: draft panels up at <link to draft>. Will iterate. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks all. Follow up async — ping here when rollout completed. :sparkles:
